paragraphs.text: Turtle-Team Up is a supplemental Magic: The Gathering box set for co-op play , that was released simultaneously with the main Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles set on March 6, 2026. The price was $49.99.

According to Corey Bowen , "A main purpose of Turtle Team-Up is to be a decent onboarding tool for an enfranchised player to teach a new player, or even a parent to teach their child". The product has similarities to the Challenge Decks that were released as part of the Hero's Path of the Theros block . In this new co-operative strategy format for Magic: The Gathering , two to four players battle for survival against an Enemy deck full of villainous adversaries. You can play with your favorite of the four pre-built 60-card hero decks, each based on one of the Turtles, or use the included Play Boosters to expand your strategies. Average game length is about 45 minutes.

Each Boss in the Enemy deck comes with its own passive ability, which remains active for as long as the Boss remains on the battlefield, and those abilities are meant to resemble common effects seen throughout Magic: The Gathering . The Event cards in the Enemy deck are also tailored toward that onboarding goal, where players have to decide as a group. "Some are increasing tempo, some are designed to be comeback mechanics, and then most importantly, there are a lot of events that ask you as a team to make a choice together," Bowen said. "That strategic conversation was really important." The final piece of the Enemy deck is the Ninjas : creatures that Bosses can use to attack the player team directly.

4 Themed decks Each deck is themed around one of the four main Turtles. Each deck consists of 60 cards, including cards from TMT and TMC . Each themed deck includes 8 new-to- Magic cards with the TMC code.
1 Enemy deck Includes 38 cards designed exclusively for the Turtle Team-Up experience using the TMC expansion code 11 Bosses 10 Creatures 17 Events
1 Punch-out counter sheet Cardboard life trackers for players (turtle shields and pizza pointers) Life tracker for Bosses +1/+1 counters
4 Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles Play Boosters

To begin, each player shuffles their deck and draws seven cards, while a Boss card is drawn from the Boss deck and turned face up onto the table. All players share a single life total, and life totals are dependent on how many players are in the game:
If there are two players, both the player group and the Boss start with 20 life.
If there are three players, the player group starts with 30 life.
If there are four players, the player group starts with 40 life, and the Boss starts with 30 life.

Each game requires the player group to successfully defeat Bosses by lowering their life total to 0. Matches play out in three stages: Stage 1 puts the group against a single Boss card, and once that Boss is defeated, it is taken out of play and replaced with two Bosses for Stage 2. If the group clears Stage 2, three Bosses are then introduced to the board for the third and final stage.

When the group clears a stage, only the defeated Bosses leave the battlefield; any Ninja creatures attacking for the Bosses remain in play, as do any creatures or other permanents in play for the player group.

The player group shares each of its turns, and they will always go first. Player turns proceed through the same phases as in a normal game of Magic: The Gathering ; they'll untap their creatures and lands, resolve any upkeep effects, and then draw a card. From there, each player can cast spells and creatures in any order, and players can discuss between themselves what order in which to play spells to maximize their effects.

After all spells are cast, the group then moves to a combat phase, where they can choose to send summoned creatures in for an attack. Damage is then calculated and applied to the Bosses' life total, after which players get a second main phase for casting spells. Once all actions have been taken, the group moves to the end step, resolves any end step effects, and then passes the turn to the Bosses.

The Boss turn plays out in three specific phases: Untap, Action, and Combat. The Untap phase untaps every Ninja card that attacked the previous turn, the Action phase will see the Bosses play Event cards, and the Combat phase will send any available Ninjas into combat against the group.

Each Action phase in a two-player game will see the Bosses play two Event cards. For each Event, one player will reveal the top card of the Event deck, resolve any game actions that result from that Event card, place the Event in the Bosses' graveyard, and then repeat the process once. In three-player or four-player games, Bosses will use three Event cards per Action phase.

After all Events have resolved, the Bosses then move to combat, and all available Ninjas will attack. The player group can then assign blockers as they so choose, and once all damage is resolved and defeated creatures are removed, the turn passes back to the player group.
This process repeats until either the player group's life total reaches zero, or the group defeats all three stages of Bosses and claim victory.
The instruction booklet that comes with Turtle Team-Up gives a few suggestions on ways to shake up the basic gameplay loop, including:
Leaving defeated Bosses in play between stages to add more Boss effects to the board
Giving Haste to all Ninjas summoned by Bosses, so they can attack on the same turn they appear
Increasing the Bosses' life total between stages
All new cards in the decks are designed with the co-op team-up play in mind. Some are aimed at Two-Headed Giant .
Every one of the four 60-card decks contains a copy of the new uncommon card Definitely Not a Turtle .
The deck is split into two parts: the bosses and the events, together with the creatures. They have non-standard card backs .
